title: 411. Trigonometry & Periodic Models: Determining Acute Angles from Trigonometric Ratios
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Acute angle from a standard sine value
questions.learningObjective: Find an acute angle from a standard value of sine.
questions.question: An acute angle \(\theta\) satisfies \(\sin\theta=\frac{1}{2}\). What is \(\theta\)?
questions.explanation: Among acute angles, \(\sin 30^\circ=\frac{1}{2}\), so \(\theta=30^\circ\). For \(60^\circ\) the sine is \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), and it is the cosine that equals \(\frac{1}{2}\).
questions.hint: Recall the sine values of the three standard acute angles and pick the angle that matches.

questions.concept: Acute angle from a standard tangent value
questions.learningObjective: Find an acute angle from a standard value of tangent.
questions.question: An acute angle \(\theta\) satisfies \(\tan\theta=1\). What is \(\theta\)?
questions.explanation: A tangent of \(1\) means the opposite and adjacent sides are equal, so the right triangle is isosceles and \(\theta=45^\circ\). For \(30^\circ\) the tangent is \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\), which is less than \(1\).
questions.hint: A tangent of \(1\) means the two legs have equal length.

questions.concept: Acute angle from a standard cosine value
questions.learningObjective: Find an acute angle from a standard value of cosine.
questions.question: An acute angle \(\theta\) satisfies \(\cos\theta=\frac{1}{2}\). What is \(\theta\)?
questions.explanation: Among acute angles, \(\cos 60^\circ=\frac{1}{2}\), so \(\theta=60^\circ\). For \(30^\circ\) the cosine is \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\); it is the sine of \(30^\circ\) that equals \(\frac{1}{2}\).
questions.hint: Be careful to use the cosine values, not the sine values, of the standard angles.

questions.learningObjective: Determine an acute angle of a right triangle from its two legs.
questions.question: In a right triangle, the side opposite an acute angle \(\theta\) is \(5\) and the side adjacent to \(\theta\) is \(5\sqrt{3}\). What is \(\theta\)?
questions.explanation: The tangent is \(\tan\theta=\frac{5}{5\sqrt{3}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\), and the acute angle with this tangent is \(30^\circ\). The angle \(60^\circ\) has tangent \(\sqrt{3}\), the reciprocal ratio.
questions.hint: Form the tangent ratio with the opposite side in the numerator and simplify it.

questions.concept: Angle from opposite side and hypotenuse
questions.learningObjective: Determine an acute angle of a right triangle from the opposite side and the hypotenuse.
questions.question: In a right triangle, the hypotenuse is \(14\) and the side opposite an acute angle \(\theta\) is \(7\sqrt{2}\). What is \(\theta\)?
questions.explanation: The sine is \(\sin\theta=\frac{7\sqrt{2}}{14}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\), and the acute angle with this sine is \(45^\circ\). For \(60^\circ\) the sine would be \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), which would need an opposite side of \(7\sqrt{3}\).
questions.hint: Compute the ratio of the opposite side to the hypotenuse and compare it with the standard sine values.

questions.concept: Angle from a decimal sine value
questions.learningObjective: Use the inverse sine to find an acute angle to one decimal place.
questions.question: An acute angle \(\theta\) satisfies \(\sin\theta=0.6\). What is \(\theta\), to one decimal place?
questions.explanation: Using the inverse sine, \(\theta=\sin^{-1}(0.6)\approx 36.87^\circ\approx 36.9^\circ\). The value \(53.1^\circ\) is \(\cos^{-1}(0.6)\), the complement of the correct angle.
questions.hint: Apply the inverse of the same function that is given; check that the result is less than \(45^\circ\) because \(0.6<\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\).

questions.learningObjective: Find the angle of inclination from a rise and a horizontal run.
questions.question: A ramp rises \(1\text{ m}\) over a horizontal distance of \(4\text{ m}\). What angle does the ramp make with the horizontal, to one decimal place?
questions.explanation: The rise is opposite the angle and the horizontal run is adjacent to it, so \(\tan\theta=\frac{1}{4}\) and \(\theta=\tan^{-1}(0.25)\approx 14.04^\circ\approx 14.0^\circ\). The value \(14.5^\circ\approx\sin^{-1}(0.25)\) would be correct only if \(4\text{ m}\) were the length of the sloping surface.
questions.hint: Decide whether the \(4\text{ m}\) is a leg or the hypotenuse before choosing the inverse function.

questions.learningObjective: Select the inverse trigonometric ratio that matches the known sides.
questions.question: In a right triangle, the side adjacent to an acute angle \(\theta\) is \(5\) and the hypotenuse is \(13\). What is \(\theta\), to one decimal place?
questions.explanation: The known sides are the adjacent side and the hypotenuse, so \(\cos\theta=\frac{5}{13}\) and \(\theta=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\right)\approx 67.38^\circ\approx 67.4^\circ\). The value \(22.6^\circ\approx\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\right)\) is the other acute angle of the triangle.
questions.hint: The adjacent side and the hypotenuse form the cosine ratio.

questions.concept: Smallest angle of a right triangle
questions.learningObjective: Identify and compute the smallest angle of a right triangle from its sides.
questions.question: A right triangle has sides \(8\), \(15\), and \(17\). What is the measure of its smallest angle, to one decimal place?
questions.explanation: The smallest angle is opposite the shortest side, \(8\). With hypotenuse \(17\), \(\sin\theta=\frac{8}{17}\) and \(\theta\approx 28.07^\circ\approx 28.1^\circ\). The value \(61.9^\circ\) is the other acute angle, opposite the side of length \(15\).
questions.hint: The smallest angle of a triangle is opposite its shortest side.

questions.learningObjective: Use the complementary-angle relation to determine an acute angle.
questions.question: An acute angle \(\theta\) satisfies \(\sin\theta=\cos 20^\circ\). What is \(\theta\)?
questions.explanation: For acute angles, \(\cos 20^\circ=\sin(90^\circ-20^\circ)=\sin 70^\circ\). Sine is increasing on acute angles, so \(\sin\theta=\sin 70^\circ\) gives \(\theta=70^\circ\). Note that \(\sin 20^\circ\approx 0.342\) while \(\cos 20^\circ\approx 0.940\), so \(\theta=20^\circ\) does not satisfy the equation.
questions.hint: The cosine of an acute angle equals the sine of its complement.
